arguments.summary: Draft synthesis at the closed-market assessment time: NVDA has the cleaner 63-session price/risk record, while MU has the stronger near-term guided operating bridge but materially higher observed path risk. Both valuation grids are explicitly hypothetical total-GAAP EPS/P-E sensitivities; unquantified policy/supply exposure and mixed macro evidence preclude an unconditional valuation-based ranking.

claims.text: The relevant market anchors are split-adjusted completed SIP closes on 2026-10-02: $233.95 for NVDA and $1,074.89 for MU. The market was closed at assessment; IEX snapshots are single-venue stale observations, not consolidated executable quotes.

NVDA has the conditional 63-session market-behavior edge over MU: it returned 19.64% versus 9.15%, exceeded SPY by 17.19 versus 6.71 percentage points and XLK by 10.79 versus 0.31 points, with a 10.58% versus 25.48% maximum close-path drawdown. This comparison does not extend to 21 sessions, where MU had the stronger XLK-relative result.

NVDA reported six-month FY2027 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.85 through 2026-07-26, but $24.14bn of other income was recorded in that period. MU reported FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33 and guided FQ1-2027 GAAP diluted EPS to $37.84 plus or minus $1.00. These figures establish different earnings anchors, not comparable recurring earnings or valuation.

NVDA's stipulated FY2027 total-GAAP sensitivity gives bear/base/bull outcomes of -38.45%/+2.59%/+53.88% from the completed close; MU's stipulated FY2027 sensitivity gives -21.85%/+11.64%/+50.71%. In each grid bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss, by 15.43 and 28.86 percentage points respectively, but neither asymmetry supplies probabilities, fair values, or a cross-stock preference.

The macro evidence is mixed: the 10-year yield rose while fed funds was flat, technology price strength coexisted with weaker IWM and HYG price performance, and no inflation, real-yield, credit-spread, FX or issuer-order series identifies the dominant regime. Accordingly, stock leadership should remain stock-specific rather than be called broad risk-on confirmation.

NVDA discloses that it is effectively foreclosed from China by export controls and depends especially on Taiwan and South Korea supply; the January rule provides conditional case-by-case licensing, not proof of approval. MU discloses that possible Section 232/301 outcomes could impose tariffs or trade restrictions. Neither issuer's reviewed disclosure quantifies the current financial effect.

A limited, conditional 63-session preference for NVDA is supported by its stronger completed-session relative performance and shallower observed path risk, not by valuation or policy superiority. It remains conditional on trend persistence and no adverse demand, policy or supply disclosure; MU remains an operating-cycle opportunity whose stronger guided near-term bridge is offset by materially greater observed path risk.

gaps.description: No observed forward P/E, consensus EPS, verified fiscal-calendar endpoint, or future diluted-share bridge is available. This prevents an unconditional valuation or relative-value ranking, although the explicit sensitivities remain conditionally usable.

Current legal status, licenses, product eligibility, geographic revenue/sourcing and financial sensitivity of export/trade measures are unquantified. This prevents sizing policy impact but not recognizing the disclosed conditional channels.
No issuer input-cost share, commodity hedge/pass-through, or current power/material disruption is evidenced. Commodity conclusions are limited to conditional operational mechanisms.

assumptions: All scenario EPS and P/E values are selected stress assumptions, not forecasts, consensus, observed multiples, fair values or probability weights.
The 63-session technical comparison uses matched split-adjusted SIP price returns through 2026-10-02 and does not predict performance over the next 63 sessions.
Policy, macro and commodity mechanisms are conditional because issuer exposure magnitude and causal attribution are unavailable.
arguments.counter_thesis: AI compute and memory demand could sustain reported/guided earnings while policy frictions remain manageable, allowing both names to continue higher despite elevated yields and extension. Conversely, demand or margin disappointment could occur alongside multiple compression, while policy/supply restrictions become realized; the sensitivities deliberately show these joint-risk cases without assigning odds.

review_conditions.description: Reassess both issuer outlooks after the next results and verified policy action: confirm whether NVDA operating earnings are durable apart from other income and whether MU's GAAP EPS/gross-margin outlook holds; a material deterioration weakens the assumed earnings bridges, while durable operating confirmation strengthens them.
A completed split-adjusted SIP NVDA close below $223.786 would weaken the near-term trend component of the conditional 63-session preference and require reassessment of relative-price persistence.
A completed split-adjusted SIP MU close below $1025.0015 would weaken its rising-trend setup and increase the relevance of its high-volatility drawdown path.

question_effects.reason: Company evidence differentiates NVDA's accelerated-computing demand/margin bridge from MU's AI-memory pricing, supply and margin-durability bridge; Macro's competing regime analysis remains conditional because orders are not measured.
Macro evidence shows mixed proxy behavior, so the 63-session technical preference is retained as stock-specific market behavior rather than broad risk-on confirmation.

NVDA.thesis: NVDA is the conditional 63-session preference because its completed-session relative strength and drawdown profile were superior to MU's. The business case depends on AI demand/margins supporting earnings without reliance on unforecasted non-operating gains.
NVDA.counter_thesis: High RSI/extension, a negative 21-session excess return versus XLK, higher long yields, and a demand/margin miss can compress the multiple. China access and Taiwan/South Korea supply are material but unquantified risk channels.
assumptions: FY2027 total-GAAP EPS/P-E grid inputs are hypothetical.
FY2027 end 2027-01-31 is an unverified assumed endpoint.
The conditional relative preference is technical, limited to 63-session behavior, and is not valuation superiority.

review_conditions.description: A completed split-adjusted SIP close below $223.786 weakens the near-term trend component and triggers a reassessment of the conditional price preference.

Review on issuer results or verified export/supply disclosure: evidence that recurring operating earnings weaken or that licenses/supply are adversely affected weakens the thesis; durable operating earnings and no material disruption strengthen it.

NVDA.valuation: FY2027 sensitivity period is 2026-01-26 to unverified assumed 2027-01-31, US GAAP and split-adjusted shares. Reported interim GAAP diluted EPS was $4.85 through 2026-07-26; no management guidance interval is supplied. Stipulated bear/base/bull total-GAAP EPS of $8/$10/$12 leave residual EPS of $3.15/$5.15/$7.15 under a constant-share approximation. At hypothetical 18x/24x/30x, sensitivity is -38.45%/+2.59%/+53.88%; base break-even is $9.7479 EPS at fixed 24x or 23.395x at fixed $10 EPS. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 15.43pp. These are joint EPS/multiple stresses, not forecasts; the reported anchor includes material other income, so they do not establish recurring operating valuation.

business.conclusion: Strong reported earnings are qualified by material other income and unmeasured demand durability.
business.qualification: Future operating earnings require separation from non-operating effects and demand/margin confirmation.

valuation.conclusion: The total-GAAP grid is a useful stated sensitivity but not an observed valuation or fair value.
valuation.qualification: No forward multiple, consensus, verified fiscal endpoint or future-share reconciliation.

market_behavior.conclusion: NVDA has the stronger 63-session completed-price record, while 21-session XLK-relative behavior is weaker.
market_behavior.qualification: Historical descriptive data only; no prediction or causality.

policy_exposure.conclusion: China/export and East-Asian supply channels are material disclosed risks; case-by-case licensing is not established access.
policy_exposure.qualification: Financial magnitude and current applicability are unknown.

relative_preference.conclusion: Conditional 63-session preference versus MU rests on market behavior, not valuation or policy superiority.
relative_preference.qualification: Reassess if trend breaks or issuer/policy evidence alters the risk balance.

global_analysis.overall_assessment: Conditional opportunity based on a cleaner 63-session technical profile, with business, valuation and policy conclusions explicitly qualified.

global_forces.mechanism: Discount-rate pressure can reprice equity multiples before order changes flow through earnings.
global_forces.consequence: Limits the valuation case despite current price strength.

global_forces.mechanism: Demand/margin realization supports operating EPS, but reported other income complicates conversion of GAAP EPS into recurring earnings.
global_forces.consequence: Next results can validate or weaken the sensitivity bridge.

global_forces.mechanism: Licensing/customer restrictions and component continuity can constrain addressable demand or delivery.
global_forces.consequence: China is optionality, not assumed revenue; supply disruption is downside.

conditional_outcomes.condition: Demand/margins disappoint, policy or supply friction worsens, and the stipulated $8 EPS/18x case applies.
conditional_outcomes.consequence: Grid sensitivity is $144, or -38.45% from the completed close.
conditional_outcomes.plausibility_basis: Policy/supply channels and multiple-risk mechanism are disclosed, but no probability is assigned.

conditional_outcomes.condition: Total-GAAP EPS reaches stipulated $10 and the selected 24x multiple holds.
conditional_outcomes.plausibility_basis: This is an explicit sensitivity assumption, not a ranked forecast.

conditional_outcomes.condition: Demand/mix durability supports stipulated $12 EPS and the selected 30x multiple.
conditional_outcomes.plausibility_basis: Requires joint earnings and multiple expansion; China sales are not assumed.

global_analysis.recommend_considering: Over 5/21/63 sessions, consider only a conditional trend-led case and monitor completed closes, next earnings quality and verified policy/supply developments. Do not treat the hypothetical grid as a target or the IEX trade as a live quote.
global_analysis.short_summary: NVDA's 63-session price record is cleaner than MU's, but valuation rests on a total-GAAP sensitivity with material non-operating-income qualification and material policy/supply uncertainty.

MU.thesis: MU has a strong reported FY2026 and explicit FQ1-2027 GAAP outlook, making its operating bridge clearer near term than NVDA's. However, sustaining it requires AI-memory demand, pricing and unusually high margins through the remaining year, while the observed 63-session path was substantially more volatile.
MU.counter_thesis: Guidance and high margins may persist, and a rising SMA20 with positive 21/63-session excess could reaccelerate. But negative five-session relative performance, high historical volatility and memory-cycle normalization mean confirmation is needed.
assumptions: FY2027 total-GAAP EPS/P-E inputs are hypothetical.
FQ1 guided midpoint is held fixed in the annual bridge; future shares are unknown.
Policy and commodity channels are unquantified conditional risks.

review_conditions.description: A completed split-adjusted SIP close below $1025.0015 weakens the rising-trend setup and elevates observed path-risk concerns.
Review next earnings if GAAP EPS or gross-margin outlook materially changes from FQ1 guidance; weaker pricing/margin guidance weakens the annual bridge, while sustained guidance strengthens it.

MU.valuation: FY2027 sensitivity period is 2026-09-04 to unverified assumed 2027-09-02, US GAAP and split-adjusted shares. FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $74.33; FQ1-2027 GAAP EPS guidance is $37.84 +/- $1.00. Holding that midpoint fixed, stipulated annual EPS of $120/$150/$180 require residual $82.16/$112.16/$142.16 over the remaining three quarters, a non-exact future-share bridge. At hypothetical 7x/8x/9x, sensitivity is -21.85%/+11.64%/+50.71%; base break-even is $134.3613 EPS at fixed 8x or 7.1659x at fixed $150 EPS. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 28.86pp. These are joint earnings/multiple stresses, not forecasts, probabilities or evidence of a fair multiple.

business.conclusion: Reported results and FQ1 guidance support a strong near-term operating backdrop, but remaining-year pricing/margin durability is unproven.
business.qualification: Memory supply response, pricing and customer demand determine whether the bridge holds.

valuation.conclusion: The explicit grid frames cycle sensitivity but does not establish current valuation.
valuation.qualification: No observed forward P/E, consensus or future-share reconciliation.

market_behavior.conclusion: Positive 21/63-session momentum coexists with five-session lag and much higher observed volatility/drawdown than NVDA.

policy_exposure.conclusion: Prospective Section 232/301 trade measures are a disclosed cost/delay/demand channel.
policy_exposure.qualification: Final applicability and impact are unknown.

relative_preference.conclusion: MU is not preferred to NVDA on the supplied 63-session risk-adjusted market evidence, despite its stronger near-term guided operating bridge.
relative_preference.qualification: This is not a valuation ranking and can reverse with earnings and renewed technical leadership.

global_analysis.overall_assessment: Watch: operating results and guidance are strong, but the continuation case requires unusually high memory margins and pricing to persist amid greater path risk.

global_forces.force: AI-memory demand, pricing and supply discipline
global_forces.mechanism: Demand/mix and supply response determine realized selling prices and margins.
global_forces.consequence: Determines whether the remaining-three-quarter EPS bridge is sustainable.

global_forces.force: Higher long yields and mixed risk backdrop
global_forces.mechanism: Multiple repricing can precede demand effects; proxy divergence does not identify the macro regime.
global_forces.consequence: Do not extrapolate price strength into a macro demand forecast.

global_forces.mechanism: Potential tariffs/restrictions can raise cost, delay manufacturing or reduce demand.
global_forces.consequence: A contingent downside channel without a measured EPS deduction.

conditional_outcomes.condition: Memory pricing/supply response normalizes margins and the stipulated $120 EPS/7x case applies.
conditional_outcomes.consequence: Grid sensitivity is $840, or -21.85% from the completed close.
conditional_outcomes.plausibility_basis: The company identifies trade and cycle risks; no probability is assigned.

conditional_outcomes.condition: AI-memory demand/pricing and margins persist, supporting stipulated $180 EPS at 9x.
conditional_outcomes.plausibility_basis: Requires continuation beyond guided Q1 and multiple expansion.

global_analysis.recommend_considering: Over 5/21/63 sessions, wait for confirmation that updated EPS/gross-margin guidance and relative-price leadership offset the high observed path risk. Treat the grid as conditional sensitivity, not an executable target.
global_analysis.short_summary: MU has strong current operating momentum and near-term guidance, but is the higher-volatility, more cycle-dependent case and therefore remains a watch rather than the conditional 63-session preference.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both issuers face semiconductor trade/supply friction that could affect demand, costs or delivery, and both are exposed to macro multiple pressure. Their specific channels and magnitude differ.
shared_exposures.qualification: Dated issuer disclosures establish mechanisms, not equal exposure weights, current financial impact or a portfolio correlation.

agent_report.work_summary: Synthesized completed Company, Macro, Technical, Geopolitics, Commodities and independent Challenger findings, retaining their stated qualifications. Used the supplied completed-session evidence and deterministic grids; no new source inspection or calculation was performed in this draft.
main_conclusions: NVDA has the cleaner conditional 63-session technical profile; MU's greater volatility and drawdown temper its strong operating momentum.
Both company valuation outputs are explicitly hypothetical total-GAAP EPS/P-E sensitivities, not fair values or probability-weighted calls.
Macro proxies are mixed, so technical leadership is stock-specific rather than broad risk-on confirmation.
Policy, supply and commodity channels are material mechanisms but have no quantified issuer impact.
The Challenger concern is retained: momentum alone cannot support an unconditional preference.
agent_report.short_summary: The draft supports a conditional 63-session NVDA preference based only on completed-price behavior, while MU is watch-worthy pending proof that exceptional memory economics persist. Valuation and policy uncertainty remain explicit.
limitations: No observed forward P/E, consensus, verified fiscal endpoints or future-share reconciliation.
No quantified policy, geographic revenue, sourcing, commodity-cost or power-capacity exposure.
IEX snapshots are not current consolidated executable quotes; all market conclusions use the 2026-10-02 completed session.
